title: Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract: Customer Catch-Up Payment on the Automated Payment Line
content:
**Servicing Policy Manual and desk system reference — Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

## Scope

This policy figures the catch-up payment a customer makes in person, through Kestrel's automated payment line, to bring a past-due retail installment contract fully up to date.

## Posting

The payment is posted under the payment posting rule: the contract must be in a payable status, the posting day follows the cutoff rule, and the channel fee of the automated phone line applies.

For a catch-up payment, and only for such a payment, the payment is recorded on the contract on its posting day with its amount, channel and purpose, and the nightly posting cycle that closes that day applies it in the product's allocation order, first to simple interest accrued over the interest accrual days at the contract APR on the product's day-basis year, then to principal until the installments due are satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal; an arrears payment an agent takes toward an extension and a good-faith payment toward an extension are recorded and applied the same way under their own policies, and every other payment is applied in the allocation order when it posts, first to simple interest accrued over the interest accrual days at the contract APR on the product's day-basis year, then to principal until the installments due are satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal, and is not posted under this policy.

## When the amount is fixed

The catch-up amount is fixed only after the installment the contract's next due date shows, when it is left unpaid past its grace period and no returned payment re-opened it, carries its late charge on the contract.

The catch-up amount is not fixed until the installment whose payment posted after its grace period ended shows its late charge in the contract's ledger.

## Making the payment

The payment is the customer's own act. The tool `submit_catch_up_payment_af77047e` belongs to the customer: the agent unlocks it with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it with `call_user_discoverable_tool` on the automated payment line. The agent reads the contract reference from the retail contract lookup and gives it to the customer.

**What one call does.** It posts one installment payment to the contract through the automated phone line with no channel fee, drawn by ACH from the customer's own bank account, on its posting day, which is today when the payment is received earlier than 8:00 p.m. Central Time on a business day and otherwise the next business day (Saturdays, Sundays and US federal holidays, with a holiday that falls on a weekend observed on the nearest weekday, are not business days), recording its amount, channel and purpose, and the contract's last payment date becomes the posting day; the split of the payment across interest, principal and fees is applied by the nightly posting cycle, not by the call. The customer hears the payment confirmation number and the amount posted.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `retail_contract_id` | the reference number of the customer's retail installment contract, which the agent reads from the retail contract lookup (`find_retail_contracts`) and gives to the customer |
| `payment_amount` | the payment amount drawn from the customer's bank account, in USD with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |
| `funding_account_last4` | the last four digits of the customer's own bank account the payment is drawn from, written as 4 digits, or empty when not applicable |

**Return.** A confirmation sentence naming the payment confirmation number (an opaque text identifier), the contract reference, the amount posted in USD with 2 decimal places and the posting day (YYYY-MM-DD). A sentence that starts with "Payment posted" means the payment is on the contract.
